To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
current velocity and habitat patch availability affect the movement patterns of two herbivores, Agapetus and Physa, differently.

1) habitat structure and current velocity influence the movement patterns of stream herbivores, 2) the influence of habitat structure on stream herbivores is more apparent in slow current velocities than in swifter flows, and 3) the influence of current velocity on stream herbivore movements is greater in smooth landscapes than in structured ones.
the movement of stream grazers is constrained by habitat availability and flow refugia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how habitat patchiness interacts with current velocity, a unique environmental element in aquatic landscapes, to affect movement patterns in streambed habitats.
understanding how habitat availability interacts with flow to affect movement patterns and net displacements of two stream grazers.
how the structure and arrangement (i.e. patchiness) of habitats in streambeds influence movement patterns of two herbivores in response to current velocity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the movement of both taxa was constrained by current velocity, which in turn affected their movement patterns.
habitat availability and flow velocity interact to shape movement patterns of stream grazers, but that this interaction is species-specific and habitat-specific.
current velocity and habitat patch distribution interact to affect movement of two benthivorous grazers in a streambed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction between landscape heterogeneity and current velocity is an important determinant of streambed animal movement, which in turn affects habitat use and population distribution.
current velocity and habitat patch availability interact to affect the movement of benthic grazes.
current velocity and habitat availability in a patchy streambed landscape interact to affect the movement patterns of benthic stream grazers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
habitat structure and the direction of flow interact to constrain movement of stream grazers, and that this constraint varies with the type of organism.
the interaction between current velocity and landscape heterogeneity affects movement of stream animals.
the interaction between habitat patchiness and water flow is a critical factor in shaping movement patterns of aquatic organisms.
